command: ETLANTIC_CP_TEST_URL=<local PostgreSQL+psycopg URL> uv run pytest -q tests/prefect/test_managed_prefect_0_58.py::test_postgresql_multiprocess_retirement_and_revision_rollback
result: Workspace-source live lifecycle test passed: 1 passed in 28.34s.
assertions: A separately supervised Prefect API process used its own PostgreSQL database; version 1 and version 2 were registered as distinct immutable deployments on a Process work pool.
A canonical submission accepted on version 1 remained pinned to that route. Draining denied new admission, and retirement waited until cancellation reconciled the accepted work as drained.

Two spawned Python processes opened independent SQLModel backends and raced to retire the same PostgreSQL-backed route. Both observed the retained, paused version 1 deployment and converged on the retired lifecycle after the revision compare-and-swap race.

A separate process exited after Prefect paused version 1 but before the route's retired-state compare-and-swap. PostgreSQL still reported draining, admissions stayed closed, and the deployment remained paused.

At that exact pause-to-retired-CAS boundary, the Prefect API was stopped and restarted; both immutable deployment revisions remained readable and verifiable, the durable route stayed draining, and a new admission was denied before retirement resumed safely.
The version 2 deployment remained active and retained after version 1 retirement; the accepted submission still referenced version 1.

After closing and reopening the SQLModel backend, the retired route and accepted route binding were still present. Re-registering the exact version 1 spec reused its original deployment ID, and guarded reactivation restored the route without changing version 2.
Lifecycle history persisted through reopen and recorded draining, retired, then active.

runtime.prefect_server: Separately supervised API process backed by a dedicated per-test PostgreSQL database

limitations: This workspace-source campaign proves API restart at the process-death cut between remote pause and the retired-state CAS; other lifecycle crash boundaries remain untested.
The campaign does not implement or qualify bounded cleanup of orphaned deployment revisions; deployments are retained for audit and rollback.
This is partial release evidence and does not qualify the final installed-wheel support matrix or remote CI.
